contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute: an issue first for anything larger, a branch and a pull request with a Conventional Commit title, which merges once every required check passes: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#workflow
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution needs: tests, the passing checks of scripts/check.sh, the coding standards and a sign-off on every commit: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
floss_license_justification: The AGPL-3.0-or-later license, which the Open Source Initiative approves: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: The AGPL-3.0-or-later license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI): https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
sites_https_justification: The repository, its issues and its releases are on GitHub, and the website on GitHub Pages, all served only over HTTPS: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests, and GitHub Discussions: searchable, with a URL for every topic and comment, open to everyone with a GitHub account and usable in any browser: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/issues
english_justification: The guides for contributors, the security policy, the governance and the forms of the issues are in English, and reports in English are welcome: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
repo_public_justification: A public Git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search
repo_track_justification: Git records every change, who made it and when; every change reaches main through a pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: The changes between releases are on main and in the pull requests: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Git, a distributed version control system, on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: release-please gives every release a version of its own, from the titles of the merged pull requests, and a tag of the same name: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning: the Conventional Commit titles of the pull requests decide the version, fix a patch, feat a minor and a breaking change a major version: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#workflow
version_tags_justification: Every release has a tag vX.Y.Z, which the release workflow signs and a ruleset keeps from moving or being deleted: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/tags
release_notes_justification: Every release has its notes in CHANGELOG.md and in its GitHub release, written in the words of a user from the entries that its pull requests bring: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
report_process_justification: SUPPORT.md says where to report a bug, ask a question or propose a feature, and the issues have forms for bugs and feature requests: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, with forms for bugs and feature requests: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/issues
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues keeps every report and its answers public and searchable: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md says how to report a vulnerability and what happens next: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: The private vulnerability reporting of GitHub, which the settings as code turn on and SECURITY.md names: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/security/advisories/new
test_justification: An automated test suite, which scripts/check.sh runs with PHPUnit and its coverage, on a computer and in the CI: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
test_invocation_justification: bash scripts/check.sh runs the tests with every other check, the same on a computer and in the CI: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The CI runs scripts/check.sh with the tests on every pull request and after every change of main, as a required check: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the policy: changes need tests, and the checks of scripts/check.sh pass: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests with every change, and the checklist of the pull request template asks for tests that cover it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
warnings_justification: scripts/check.sh runs ShellCheck, php-cs-fixer, Psalm, the Lint workflow actionlint, markdownlint and REUSE, and zizmor audits the workflows: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
warnings_fixed_justification: A warning of ShellCheck, php-cs-fixer, Psalm, actionlint, markdownlint or REUSE fails a required check, scripts/check.sh in the CI or the Lint workflow, so a pull request merges only once it is fixed; the findings of zizmor go to code scanning, where the Findings workflow fails until each is fixed or accepted with its reason: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered over HTTPS, from GitHub and from the Nextcloud App Store, with an attestation of GitHub and the build provenance signed with Sigstore, which gh release verify checks: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP: the attestations and the signed provenance come from GitHub and Sigstore over HTTPS.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub's secret scanning with push protection stops a known kind of secret before it lands, and Gitleaks scans every pull request and, every week, the whole history: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL analyzes the code and the workflows on every pull request, after every change of main and every week, and Psalm with its taint analysis the PHP, which CodeQL doesn't know; ShellCheck checks the shell scripts: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs its security-extended queries, which look for the weaknesses of the CWE Top 25, Psalm's taint analysis follows untrusted input to HTML, SQL, shells and files, and zizmor audits the workflows for their security: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: A new alert of CodeQL of high or critical severity stops the merge of the pull request that adds it, and the Findings workflow fails while a finding is open that isn't accepted with its reason: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#findings-of-code-scanning
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request, after every change of main and every week: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
dco_justification: Every commit carries a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off: the check DCO of the Lint workflow fails without one, and the settings as code require it for commits made on github.com: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes how decisions are made, who has which access and who has the final responsibility: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: A code of conduct in the spirit of the Contributor Covenant 2.1, in the standard location, with private reporting: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md defines the roles maintainer, contributor, reporter and bots with their responsibilities: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 2: the maintainer and the successor designated through GitHub's account successor setting: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
documentation_current_justification: The documentation changes in the pull request that changes what it describes, as the checklist of the pull request template asks, and the website is built and checked on every change: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
sites_password_security_justification: The sites of the project are on GitHub and GitHub Pages; the project stores no passwords.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process: private reporting, an acknowledgement within 7 days, a first assessment within 14 days, a fix within 90 days at the latest and the disclosure in an advisory: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the coding standards that contributions follow: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards
coding_standards_enforced_justification: scripts/check.sh and the Lint workflow check the coding standards on every pull request, which merges only when they pass: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
installation_development_quick_justifica: CONTRIBUTING.md shows how to run every check with bash scripts/check.sh, and the dev container in .devcontainer/ has every tool set up, for VS Code and GitHub Codespaces: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
external_dependencies_justification: composer.json lists the direct dependencies, and composer.lock pins each: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/composer.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate updates the dependencies, an update that fixes a vulnerability at once, and OSV-Scanner checks every lock file in the pull requests that change one, after every change of main and every week: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Every dependency comes from its package manager, pinned in a lock file, every action by its commit hash and every image by its digest, and Renovate updates them: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#automation
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The CI runs scripts/check.sh with the whole test suite on every pull request and after every change of main, and reports its success or failure as a required check: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the written policy: changes need tests in the automated test suite, and the checks of scripts/check.sh pass: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
signed_releases_justification: Every release is immutable, GitHub signs an attestation that ties its tag to its commit and to every file, and the release workflow signs the build provenance of every file with Sigstore, without a long-lived key; SECURITY.md shows how to verify both: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: The release workflow signs every release tag without a key with gitsign, and builds no release on a tag that it didn't sign: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-the-project-keeps-itself-secure
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, lets a change reach main only through a pull request, with no exception, not even for administrators: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, keeps everybody from deleting main or force-pushing it, with no exception: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow writes an untrusted value, such as the title of a pull request or the text of an issue, into a script: each one reaches it as an environment variable, and zizmor's audit of template injection checks every workflow: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: The workflows of a pull request run with a read-only token and without secrets, every secret is in an environment that only main may use, and the workflows of outside contributors wait for the maintainer's approval: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
osps_br_03_01_justification: The channels of the project, the repository with its issues, discussions and releases on GitHub and the website on GitHub Pages, are served only over HTTPS: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed over HTTPS, from GitHub and from the Nextcloud App Store, with an attestation of GitHub and the build provenance signed with Sigstore, which gh release verify checks: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub's secret scanning with push protection, which the settings as code turn on, stops a known kind of secret before it lands, and Gitleaks scans every pull request and, every week, the whole history: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the form for bugs say how to report a defect: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests, and GitHub Discussions, open to everyone, for proposed changes and for problems of use: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/issues
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the AGPL-3.0-or-later license, which the Open Source Initiative approves: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released assets are under the AGPL-3.0-or-later license of the source code, which the Open Source Initiative approves: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license is in the file LICENSE of the repository, and REUSE.toml gives the license of every file: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Every release contains the file LICENSE: the source code of its tag, which GitHub attaches to the release, holds it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public at a static URL: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records every change, who made it and when, and the history of main is public: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: composer.json lists the direct dependencies, and composer.lock pins each: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/composer.json
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact, the private vulnerability reporting of GitHub, which reaches the maintainers that GOVERNANCE.md lists: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The token of a workflow may only read by default, a setting of the settings as code, and every workflow sets read-only or no permissions at its top: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/repository.toml
osps_br_02_01_justification: release-please gives every release a version of its own and a tag of the same name: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/releases
osps_br_04_01_justification: Every release has its notes in CHANGELOG.md and in its GitHub release, with every change for users and every security fix: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Every dependency is installed with the standard tools of its ecosystem from a lock file, pinned by version and hash, every action by its commit hash and every image by its digest: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
osps_br_06_01_justification: GitHub signs an attestation of every release with the SHA-256 digest of each of its files, and the release workflow signs the build provenance of every file with Sigstore: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the people with access to the repository, the releases and the security advisories: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#maintainers-and-access
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the roles maintainer, contributor, reporter and bots with their responsibilities: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution needs: tests, the passing checks, the coding standards and a sign-off on every commit: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit carries a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off, with which its author asserts the right to contribute it: the check DCO fails without one, and the settings as code require it for commits made on github.com: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The ruleset of main lets a pull request merge only once every required check of the settings as code has passed on the latest main, with no exception: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/repository.toml
osps_qa_06_01_justification: A required check runs scripts/check.sh with the test suite on every pull request before it can merge: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md has the policy of coordinated disclosure with its times: an acknowledgement within 7 days, a first assessment within 14 days, a fix within 90 days at the latest, and the disclosure with the fixed release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
osps_vm_03_01_justification: The private vulnerability reporting of GitHub, which SECURITY.md names: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: A fixed vulnerability is published in a GitHub security advisory and in the release notes, as SECURITY.md says: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow starts with read-only or no permissions, and each job gets only those that it needs; zizmor audits the permissions of every workflow: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: The inputs of a workflow, also those of collaborators, reach its scripts only as environment variables, never in the text of a script, which zizmor's audit of template injection checks: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every file of a release is attached to the immutable release of its tag, which the attestation of GitHub ties to it, and its SBOMs carry the version of the release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md shows how to verify the integrity and the authenticity of a release with gh release verify: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_do_03_02_justification: The certificate of Sigstore names the release workflow of the repository as the author of a release, and SECURITY.md shows how to check it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md: security fixes are provided for the latest release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release gets security fixes, so a release gets none once the next one is published: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release carries SBOMs of what it ships, as SPDX and as CycloneDX: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says how to run the tests, with bash scripts/check.sh and before every push with the hook, and the CI runs them on every pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the policy: changes need tests, and the checks of scripts/check.sh pass: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
osps_vm_04_02_justification: When the project accepts an advisory in osv-scanner.toml, with its reason, the release carries an OpenVEX document that tells scanners that the advisory doesn't affect it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md sets the threshold: a new alert of CodeQL of high or critical severity, or a new error, stops the merge, and the Findings workflow fails while a finding is open that isn't accepted with its reason: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/SECURITY.md#findings-of-code-scanning
osps_vm_06_02_justification: CodeQL analyzes every pull request as a required check, and the ruleset of main stops the merge of one that adds an alert of high or critical severity; a finding is accepted only with its reason in .github/findings.toml: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search/blob/main/.github/findings.toml
